span.label: existence
span.quote: Applying the machinery of allegories then yields that KHausR is equivalent to DeVS, thus resolving a problem recently raised in the literature.

span.label: de Vries duality for compact Hausdorff spaces
span.quote: In [12] de Vries generalized Stone duality to a duality for the category KHaus of compact Hausdorffspaces and continuous maps.

span.label: mathematical-proof
span.quote: We prove that in both DeVS and GleR isomorphisms are structure-preserving bijections.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Realising compact Hausdorff spaces as quotients of Stone spaces by closed equivalence relations, and then splitting those equivalences as idempotents inside the allegory, transports the Stone-space/boolean-algebra equivalence up to the compact Hausdorff/de Vries level.
span.quote: We will obtain a category equivalent to KHausR by splitting closed equivalence relations in StoneR, a construction that we describe in the language of allegories.

span.label: One of the intermediate categories the construction produces has badly behaved isomorphisms.
span.quote: One drawback of StoneER is that isomorphisms are not structure-preserving bijections.

span.label: In one of the categories used, two objects can be isomorphic while differing in cardinality, so the word does not carry its usual force there.
span.note: what this limits: a statement that two objects of StoneER are isomorphic: isomorphism there is not a structure-preserving bijection, and two objects may be isomorphic even without sharing the same cardinality
span.quote: Not every isomorphism in StoneER is a structure-preserving bijection; two objects (X1, E1) and (X2, E2) may be isomorphic even if

span.label: The composition operation in the classical dual category is not the usual function composition, which is the drawback the paper exists to remove.
span.note: what this limits: any argument that composes morphisms in de Vries' original dual category DeV: composition there is not usual function composition, whereas in the alternative proposed here it is usual relation composition
span.quote: One drawback of DeV is that composition of morphisms is not usual function composition

span.label: The direction chosen for the morphisms is declared a matter of taste, with the opposite convention giving a dual statement of the same result.
span.note: what this limits: the direction in which this equivalence is stated: the authors call the choice of direction a matter of taste and note the result can equally be stated as a dual equivalence
span.quote: Thus, the choice of direction of morphisms is ultimately a matter of taste and the equivalence can alternatively be stated as a dual equivalence

span.label: de Vries algebras
span.quote: The objects of the dual category DeV are complete boolean algebras equipped with a proximity relation, known as de Vries algebras

span.label: closed relation
span.quote: morphisms are closed relations (i.e., relations R : X → Y such that R is a closed subset of X

span.label: isomorphism
span.quote: Not every isomorphism in StoneER is a structure-preserving bijection

span.label: structure-preserving bijection
span.quote: One drawback of StoneER is that isomorphisms are not structure-preserving bijections

span.label: subordination relations
span.quote: Similarly, splitting equivalences in BAS yields a category that is equivalent to the category DeVS of de Vries algebras and compatible subordination relations

span.label: isomorphism - IN StoneER, NOT A BIJECTION: two objects may be isomorphic even when their underlying spaces differ in cardinality, so the word here does not imply the structure-preserving correspondence a reader would assume
span.quote: Not every isomorphism in StoneER is a structure-preserving bijection; two objects (X1, E1) and (X2, E2) may be isomorphic even if X1 and X2 do not share the same cardinality

span.label: isomorphism - IN DeVS AND GleR, RECOVERED: the paper proves that in these two categories isomorphisms ARE structure-preserving bijections, which is what makes them the better home for the duality
span.quote: We prove that in both DeVS and GleR isomorphisms are structure-preserving bijections

span.label: composition - THE ORDINARY OPERATION OR NOT: in de Vries' original category it is not usual function composition; in the approach proposed here it is usual relation composition, and that difference is given as the advantage
span.quote: One advantage of this approach is that composition of morphisms is usual relation composition

span.label: extends → de Vries duality [12]
span.quote: In this paper we propose an alternative approach to de Vries duality, where morphisms between de Vries algebras become certain relations and composition is usual relation composition.

span.label: extends → the open problem raised in [5, Rem. 3.14]
span.quote: This resolves the problem raised in [5, Rem. 3.14] to find a generalization of the category of de Vries algebras that is (dually) equivalent to KHausR.

span.label: builds-on → Celani [11]'s quasi-semi-homomorphisms and the subordination relations of [4]
span.quote: We show that such functions correspond to subordination relations between A and B studied in [4].

span.label: isomorphism —distinct-from→ structure-preserving bijection
span.quote: Not every isomorphism in StoneER is a structure-preserving bijection; two objects (X1, E1) and (X2, E2) may be isomorphic even if X1 and X2 do not share the same cardinality

span.label: Stone duality lifts to an equivalence between Stone spaces with closed relations and boolean algebras with subordination relations.
span.quote: Stone duality generalizes to an equivalence between the categories StoneR of Stone spaces and closed relations and BAS of boolean algebras and subordination relations.

span.label: Splitting the equivalences (closed equivalence relations) in the allegory of Stone spaces and closed relations produces a category equivalent to compact Hausdorff spaces with closed relations.
span.quote: Splitting equivalences in StoneR yields a category that is equivalent to the category KHausR of compact Hausdorffspaces and closed relations.

span.label: Splitting the equivalences on the algebraic side produces a category equivalent to de Vries algebras with compatible subordination relations.
span.quote: Similarly, splitting equivalences in BAS yields a category that is equivalent to the category DeVS of de Vries algebras and compatible subordination relations.

span.label: Compact Hausdorff spaces with closed relations are equivalent to de Vries algebras with compatible subordinations, settling the open problem of finding a de Vries-style dual for KHausR.
span.quote: Applying the machinery of allegories then yields that KHausR is equivalent to DeVS, thus resolving a problem recently raised in the literature.

span.label: That equivalence cuts down to an equivalence between compact Hausdorff spaces with continuous maps and the wide subcategory DeVF of de Vries algebras whose morphisms obey two extra conditions, giving an alternative to de Vries duality.
span.quote: The equivalence between KHausR and DeVS further restricts to an equivalence between the category KHaus of compact Hausdorffspaces and continuous functions and the wide subcategory DeVF of DeVS whose morphisms satisfy additional conditions.

span.label: The gain over classical de Vries duality is that composition of morphisms becomes ordinary composition of relations rather than the ad hoc de Vries composition.
span.quote: One advantage of this approach is that composition of morphisms is usual relation composition.

span.label: The equivalence is realised concretely by sending a closed relation R to the subordination on regular opens defined by U S V exactly when R maps the closure of U inside V.
span.quote: The key is to associate with each closed relation R : X → Y the relation SR : RO(X) → RO(Y ) given by U SR V ⇐⇒ R[cl(U )] ⊆ V

span.label: Isomorphisms in the intermediate categories are badly behaved: two S5-subordination spaces can be isomorphic in StoneER while their underlying Stone spaces differ in cardinality.
span.quote: Not every isomorphism in StoneER is a structure-preserving bijection; two objects (X1, E1) and (X2, E2) may be isomorphic even if X1 and X2 do not share the same cardinality.

span.label: In the de Vries algebra category DeVS, by contrast, every isomorphism is a structure-preserving bijection.
span.quote: Isomorphisms in DeVS are given by structure-preserving bijections.

span.label: The new category DeVF is dually isomorphic to the classical category DeV of de Vries algebras and de Vries morphisms, so classical de Vries duality is recovered from the new one.
span.quote: The contravariant functors described in Definition 6.13 establish a dual isomorphism between DeVF and DeV.

span.label: The construction yields, as a by-product, a new proof that the category of compact Hausdorff spaces is the exact completion of the category of Stone spaces.
span.quote: Thus, as a consequence we obtain an alternative proof of the fact that KHaus is the exact completion of Stone.

span.label: closed relation between Stone spaces
span.quote: If X, Y are Stone spaces, then we call R : X → Y closed if R is a closed subset of X × Y

span.label: quasi-semi-homomorphism
span.quote: A quasi-semi-homomorphism is a function ∆ : A → J (B) such that ∆(1) = B and ∆(a ∧ b) = ∆(a) ∩ ∆(b) for all a, b ∈ A.

span.label: subordination relation
span.quote: A subordination relation from a boolean algebra A to a boolean algebra B is a relation S : A → B satisfying, for a, b ∈ A and c, d ∈ B:

span.label: allegory
span.quote: An allegory A is an order-enriched dagger category such that: (i) each partially ordered hom-set of A has binary meets;

span.label: S5-subordination
span.quote: An S5-subordination is a subordination S : B → B satisfying conditions (S5)–(S7).

span.label: S5-subordination space
span.quote: an object of StoneER is a pair (X, E) where X is a Stone space and E is a closed equivalence relation on X. We call such pairs S5-subordination spaces.

span.label: extremally disconnected space
span.quote: A topological space is extremally disconnected if the closure of each open set is open.

span.label: Gleason space
span.quote: A Gleason space is an object (X, E) of StoneER such that X is extremally disconnected and E is irreducible

span.label: de Vries algebra
span.quote: The objects of the dual category DeV are complete boolean algebras equipped with a proximity relation, known as de Vries algebras.
